questions.topic: Why Sparse and Dense Retrieval Fail Differently

questions.question: What is dense retrieval's characteristic weakness?

It requires labeled relevance judgments to rank

questions.topic: Why Sparse and Dense Retrieval Fail Differently

k divided by r

Length-normalized raw scores

Rank positions only

About 0.0323
About 0.0610
About 0.1640

questions.topic: Reciprocal Rank Fusion
questions.question: With k = 60, document A ranks 1st and 6th in two lists while document B ranks 2nd in both. Which fuses higher and why?

questions.topic: Reciprocal Rank Fusion
questions.question: What is the effect of raising the RRF constant k?

questions.topic: Reciprocal Rank Fusion
questions.question: When is weighted RRF justified over plain RRF?
options: Whenever the scores are heavy-tailed
When one retriever has lower latency

options: Spreads the remaining scores evenly
Centers every score around zero mean
Compresses almost all scores into the bottom of the range
Converts every score into a rank position

questions.topic: Score Normalization vs Rank Fusion
questions.question: Why is rank fusion invariant to score scale?
options: Any monotone transformation of scores leaves ranks unchanged
It recomputes corpus statistics for every query
It normalizes scores by document length first

questions.topic: Score Normalization vs Rank Fusion
questions.question: When can score fusion beat rank fusion?

When models are swapped frequently
When score distributions are heavy-tailed

questions.topic: Score Normalization vs Rank Fusion
questions.question: Why is thresholding on min-max fused scores unsound?
options: Thresholds require integer-valued scores
Each query's fused scale is different
Fusion weights depend on the threshold
